description: Measures the linear correlation between configuration fitness and Euclidean distance to the global optimal solution, reflecting the global guidance of the search space
calculation_method: Calculated using the calculate_fitness_distance_correlation function from the pflacco library: 1) Take the real global optimal solution (configuration with min/max fitness) in the sample as the benchmark; 2) Compute the Euclidean distance from each sample to the global optimal solution; 3) Calculate the Pearson correlation coefficient between fitness values and distances by dividing the covariance of fitness and distance by the product of their standard deviations; 4) Return 0.5 if the calculation result is NaN
value_significance: Range: [-1, 1]. 1) FDC<0: Closer to the optimal solution means better fitness, with strong global guidance and easier to find the optimal solution via global search; 2) FDC>0: Closer to the optimal solution means worse fitness, with weak guidance; 3) Values closer to 0 indicate weaker correlation, leading to weaker global guidance but higher tuning flexibility for complex dual-domain scenarios.

description: Measures the average minimum mixed distance from all sample configurations to the real global optimal solutions, reflecting the global accessibility of the optimal solution
calculation_method: 1) Identify the real global optimal solutions (all configurations with optimal fitness) in the sample; 2) For each sample configuration, calculate its mixed distance to all optimal solutions (Hamming distance for categorical parameters, Euclidean distance for continuous/discrete parameters, all standardized by parameter type); 3) Take the minimum distance from each sample to the optimal solutions and calculate the average of these minimum distances for all samples; 4) Return 0.5 if there are no optimal solutions
value_significance: No fixed range, with non-negative values. Smaller values mean most sample configurations are closer to the real global optimal solution, with stronger global accessibility of the optimal solution, lower search difficulty for the tuner, and easier to find the optimal solution.

description: The proportion of local optimal solutions in the sample, reflecting the multimodality of the search space (higher proportion means more peaks)
calculation_method: 1) Generate one-dimensional mutation neighborhoods for each configuration (only a single parameter is modified, with the number of neighbors limited by max_neighbors=5); 2) Neighborhood generation rules: take nearby values after sorting for continuous parameters, randomly select for categorical/discrete parameters, and only retain neighborhood configurations existing in the sample; 3) A configuration is a local optimal solution if its fitness is not worse than all existing neighborhood configurations (≤ for minimization, ≥ for maximization); 4) Divide the number of local optimal solutions by the total number of sampled configurations to get the proportion
value_significance: Range: [0, 1]. Smaller values mean fewer local optimal solutions, the search space is closer to unimodal, lower risk of falling into local optima during tuning, and easier to find the global optimal solution; larger values mean stronger multimodality and higher tuning difficulty.

description: Describes the asymmetry of the fitness value distribution, reflecting the balance of the fitness distribution in the search space
calculation_method: Calculated using the calculate_ela_distribution function from the pflacco library: 1) Compute the base skewness as the ratio of the third moment to the cube of the second moment of fitness values; 2) Apply the MINITAB/BMDP type 3 adjustment by scaling with (1 - 1/n)^(3/2) (n is the number of samples) to get the final skewness
value_significance: Range: (-∞, ∞). Values closer to 0 indicate a more symmetric fitness distribution, leading to more stable fitness improvement/decline trends during tuning without obvious one-sided extreme value bias (suitable for dual-domain data distribution characteristics); positive values mean right skew, negative values mean left skew.

description: Describes the kurtosis (peak steepness/tail thickness) of the fitness value distribution, reflecting the concentration of extreme fitness values
calculation_method: Calculated using the calculate_ela_distribution function from the pflacco library: 1) Compute the base kurtosis as the ratio of the fourth moment to the square of the second moment of fitness values; 2) Apply the MINITAB/BMDP type 3 adjustment by scaling with (1 - 1/n)^2 and subtracting 3 (n is the number of samples) to get the final kurtosis (the kurtosis of normal distribution is 0)
value_significance: Range: (-∞, ∞). Values closer to 0 indicate a fitness distribution closer to the normal distribution, leading to lower risk of encountering extreme fitness values during tuning and stronger stability of the search process; positive values mean leptokurtic distribution (concentrated extreme values), negative values mean platykurtic distribution (scattered extreme values).

description: Reflects the correlation length of fitness values in the search space, i.e., the continuous distribution range of configurations with similar fitness
calculation_method: 1) Sort samples by their mixed distance to the optimal solution and start random walks from the real global optimal solution; 2) Dynamically increase the neighborhood radius k from 0.1 until non-self neighborhoods are found, and generate a fitness path with a fixed 50 steps for each walk; 3) Repeat sampling 50 times, calculate the first-order autocorrelation coefficient of each path and standardize it by dividing by the square of the fitness standard deviation; 4) Calculate the final value using the formula -1/log(abs(average autocorrelation coefficient)); 5) Return 0.5 in abnormal cases (no valid samples, autocorrelation coefficient is 0 or its absolute value ≥1)
value_significance: Non-negative values. Larger values mean a wider distribution range of configurations with correlated fitness and a smoother search space; larger values enable the results of local neighborhood exploration to be extended to a wider range during tuning, which is more suitable for efficient tuning of large search spaces.

description: Measures the maximum information entropy of the fitness distribution in the search space, reflecting the uncertainty and complexity of fitness changes
calculation_method: Calculated using the calculate_information_content function from the pflacco library: 1) Sort samples via the nearest neighbor strategy to generate a tour through the search space and calculate the ratio of fitness differences to distances between adjacent configurations on the tour; 2) Count the entropy of fitness transition patterns and take the maximum entropy value (ic.h_max) as the result
value_significance: Range: [0, ∞). Smaller values mean lower information uncertainty in the search space and stronger predictability of fitness changes with configuration adjustments, enabling more accurate judgment of exploration directions during tuning; larger values mean more random fitness changes and higher tuning difficulty.

description: Measures the local agglomeration and accessibility of better solutions in the search space, reflecting the difficulty of finding better solutions via local exploration
calculation_method: Calculated using the calculate_nbc function from the pflacco library: 1) Identify the nearest neighbor configuration and the nearest better configuration (neighborhood configuration with not worse fitness) for each sample configuration; 2) Calculate the ratio of [nearest neighbor distance / nearest better distance] for each sample and take the average of these ratios for all samples (nbc.nn_nb.mean_ratio) as the result
value_significance: Range: [0, ∞). Smaller values mean better solutions are closer relative to the nearest neighbor configurations and better solutions are locally agglomerated in the search space, leading to lower difficulty in finding better solutions via local exploration during tuning (suitable for local exploration strategies of dual-domain search spaces); larger values mean more scattered distribution of better solutions and lower efficiency of local exploration.
